_what: The programs this Mac fetches on first use instead of carrying them in the app (computer/helper-runtimes.mjs). A helper is a row in `helpers`: `url` (https) to fetch, `blake3` (64 hex characters) the bytes must hash to, `size` the most bytes accepted, `file` the name it is kept under, `executable`, an optional `arch` (process.arch) it is for, and an optional `withdrawn_at` (an ISO time after which the Mac refuses to run it and says so). A row with no pinned `blake3` or `size` is refused, never fetched on trust. Nothing here names a program: a new helper is a new row, and an empty list fetches nothing. `blocked` rows ({ blake3, reason }) name content that must not run: `recheck` disables every installed helper whose bytes are blocked, with the reason, and restores it to what it was when the block is lifted. A helper row may carry `verify` (argument arrays, `{app}` filled in as the unpacked entry; any non-zero exit refuses the install before anything is moved in; so an unpinned helper is still checked for its publisher's signature). A helper row may also carry `signer` and its `url` is its source; both go in the receipt kept beside each install. A row with `unpinned: true` and no `blake3` is fetched within `size` (or `unpinned_max_bytes`) and its receipt says `pinned: false`; `adopt` lists paths of a copy the person installed themselves, used as it is; `archive: "zip"` with `entry` unpacks a zip and hands out the entry. `manifest` ({ url, signature_url, channel }, null while no list is followed) names a published list; `refresh` takes from it, after the signature is verified by a trusted key (computer/signed-manifest.json), only a strictly newer version of a helper, as { id, version, url, size, blake3, file, ... } entries.

helpers.what: The program that serves models on this Mac (Ollama).

words.unknown: This Mac has no helper named {id}. See the list for the ones it keeps.
words.unpinned: The helper {id} has no pinned hash and size, so it is not fetched.
words.wrong_machine: The helper {id} is for {arch} Macs; this one is {here}.
words.withdrawn: The helper {id} was withdrawn on {at} and is not run.
words.insecure: The helper {id} is not offered over https, so it is not fetched.
words.too_big: The helper {id} is larger than the {size} bytes it is pinned to.
words.not_verified: The helper {id} did not pass its check, so it was not installed.
words.wrong_bytes: The helper {id} did not match its pinned hash, so it was not installed.
words.fetch_failed: The helper {id} could not be fetched: {error}
words.installed: The helper {id} is installed and matches its pinned hash.
words.blocked_now: Turned off {count} blocked helper(s); turned on {restored} whose block was lifted.
words.adopted: The helper {id} you installed yourself at {path} is used as it is.
words.installed_unpinned: The helper {id} is installed. Its publisher offers nothing to check it against, so it was not verified.
words.no_manifest: This Mac follows no published helper list, so nothing was fetched.
words.refreshed: Took {count} newer helper(s) from the signed list.
